errors.unauthorized: Not signed in or session expired.
errors.forbidden: Your role is not allowed to do this.
errors.step_up_required: This action requires confirming with your passkey again.
errors.token_invalid: The token is invalid, expired or already used.
errors.rate_limited: Too many attempts. Please wait a moment.
errors.lockout_protection: Refused because it would lock you out.
errors.helper_unavailable: The system service is not reachable.
errors.unavailable: This is not possible right now.
errors.csrf_failed: Security check failed. Please reload the page.
errors.passkey_cancelled: The passkey operation was cancelled or failed.
errors.webauthn_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys.
errors.conflict: Conflict: the item already exists or was changed.
errors.permission_denied: Permission denied: your user's Linux permissions do not allow this.
errors.already_exists: An entry with this name already exists.
errors.symlink_refused: For security reasons symbolic links are not followed. Open the target directly.
errors.no_space: Not enough space on the disk.
errors.read_only_fs: The file system is mounted read-only.
errors.busy: The file is currently in use.
errors.path_blocked: This path belongs to Daemonica itself and is blocked in the file manager.
errors.sensitive_path: This is a sensitive file and needs an additional confirmation.
errors.protected_path: This path is protected and cannot be deleted, moved or renamed.
errors.virtual_fs: Files below /proc, /sys and /dev can only be viewed.
errors.limit_exceeded: The operation exceeds a limit (count, size or duration).
errors.not_supported: This is not supported on this system.
errors.not_regular_file: This is not a regular file.
errors.range_not_satisfiable: The requested range lies outside the file.
errors.mount_point: The operation would affect another mounted file system and was refused.
errors.root_mode_required: Root mode must be active for this.
errors.no_login_shell: This Linux user has no login shell.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your passkey – no password.
login.recovery: Lost your passkey? Recovery is only possible on the server: sudo daemonica-admin recover <account>

token.label: Setup token
token.help: Create the token on the server with: sudo daemonica-admin bootstrap
token.explain: The token proves you have access to the server. It is valid for 60 minutes and is consumed when the first passkey is registered.

domain.label: Dashboard domain
domain.help: The domain's DNS record must point to this server.
domain.explain: Passkeys are bound to the domain. That is why the first passkey is registered on the final domain.

allowlist.label: Allowed networks (one address or CIDR per line)
allowlist.help: Only connections from these networks are accepted – before the TLS handshake.
allowlist.publicWarning: Public means anyone on the Internet can see and attack the login page. Fixed networks, a VPN or an SSH tunnel are recommended.
allowlist.publicConfirm: I understand the risk and want to make the dashboard publicly reachable.
allowlist.explain: The default is “allowed networks only”. Local access (127.0.0.1, ::1) always remains allowed.

certificate.acmeHelp: Free, automatically issued certificate. Port 80 must briefly be free and reachable from the Internet.
certificate.staging: Let’s Encrypt Staging (testing only, not trusted by browsers)
certificate.tos: I accept the Let’s Encrypt terms of service.
certificate.working: Issuing certificate … this can take up to a minute.
certificate.explain: The dashboard only speaks TLS 1.3. The certificate is stored only for the web service.

switch.title: Switching to the final address
switch.text: The service restarts now and will be reachable at {{url}}. Open that address and enter the token again to register your first passkey.

passkey.linuxUserHelp: File access and the terminal run with this user's permissions. root is not allowed.
passkey.noUsers: There is no regular Linux user on the server. Create one first: sudo adduser <name>
passkey.name: Passkey name (e.g. laptop)
passkey.explain: Your device creates a key pair. The private key never leaves your device; the server stores only the public key.

done.title: All set!
done.text: The dashboard is set up and you are signed in. Register a second passkey next so you cannot lock yourself out.

recovery.title: Recover access
recovery.intro: Enter the token from “sudo daemonica-admin recover” and register a new passkey.

stepup.title: Confirm with passkey
stepup.text: This action is security-relevant. Confirm it with your passkey. The confirmation is valid for 5 minutes.

overview.title: Overview
overview.rebootRequired: A restart is required to complete updates.
overview.certExpiring_one: The dashboard certificate expires in {{count}} day.
overview.certExpiring_other: The dashboard certificate expires in {{count}} days.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: Passkeys are your only sign-in method. Register at least two, e.g. laptop and phone.
passkeys.secondHint: Register a second passkey – without it, only server-side recovery helps if you lose this one.
passkeys.lastOne: The last passkey cannot be removed.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.intro: See where you are signed in and end sessions. Sessions end automatically after 30 minutes of inactivity or at the latest after 12 hours.

invite.title: Accept invitation
invite.intro: An admin invited you to Daemonica. Register your passkey now – from then on you sign in with it only.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.intro: Dashboard accounts, their roles and mapped Linux users. Changes require passkey confirmation and end the affected account's sessions.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.inviteOnce: This link is shown only now and is valid once until {{time}}. Share it over a secure channel.
accounts.inviteExplain: Daemonica creates the account without a passkey and a one-time link (valid for 60 minutes). Whoever opens the link registers the first passkey for exactly this account. The token sits in the link fragment (#), so it is not sent to the server or logged until it is redeemed. The account acts with the rights of the chosen Linux user; root can never be mapped.
accounts.confirmRole: Change the role of “{{name}}”? All sessions of this account will be ended.
accounts.confirmDelete: Type “{{name}}” to delete. Passkeys and sessions are removed; the Linux user is left unchanged.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: All security-relevant events, tamper-evident through a SHA-256 hash chain. Newest first.

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: Access and behaviour of the dashboard. Risky changes are first shown as a plan, then applied and must be confirmed within 90 seconds – otherwise the server reverts them automatically.
settings.publicWarn: The dashboard is publicly reachable. Restricting it to known networks or a VPN is recommended.
settings.newListHelp: One entry per line as IP or CIDR, e.g. 203.0.113.5/32 or 2001:db8::/48. Loopback is always allowed.
settings.lockoutAck: I understand: my current IP {{ip}} will no longer be allowed. Without a confirmation from an allowed network the change is reverted after 90 seconds.
settings.publicAck: I deliberately want to make the dashboard publicly reachable.
settings.confirmPrompt: The new allowlist is active. Confirm within {{seconds}} s that you can still reach the dashboard; otherwise it is reverted automatically.
settings.rolledBackTimeout: No confirmation received – the server restored the previous allowlist.

risk.medium: Medium risk: networks that are removed lose access immediately.
risk.high: High risk: your own connection will be locked out.

settings.explain: Daemonica checks the allowlist when a connection is accepted, before TLS, and again on every request. After applying, the server closes your connection; the confirmation must arrive over a new connection and thereby proves you still get in with the new allowlist. The revert timer runs in the privileged helper – independent of the browser and the web process.
settings.moreLater: More settings (switch certificate, session lifetime, language) will follow.

services.title: Services
services.intro: systemd units on this server. Click a name for status, journal, unit file and dependencies.
services.protectedWarning: {{unit}} is a protected system service. Changing it may interrupt SSH or the dashboard. Continue? (You will confirm with your passkey.)
services.protectedHint: Protected service: changes for admins only, after passkey confirmation.
services.selfText: The dashboard will no longer be reachable. You can only start it again via SSH: sudo systemctl start daemonica-web

logs.title: Logs
logs.intro: System journal (journald). Filter by service, priority and time; search runs on the server.
logs.truncated: Result truncated – narrow the search or increase the line count.

processes.title: Processes
processes.intro: Running processes, refreshed every 3 seconds. Protected processes (e.g. PID 1, SSH, Daemonica) cannot be signalled.
processes.truncated: List truncated (too many processes) – the busiest are shown.

sig.KILL: Kill immediately – unsaved data is lost

users.title: Users
users.intro: Linux users and groups on this server. Changes require admin rights and a passkey confirmation.
users.advanced: Advanced: show and change system users
users.name: Name
users.grantSudoConfirm: {{name}} will get full administrator rights (root via sudo). Continue?
users.revokeSudoConfirm: {{name}} will lose administrator rights via sudo. Continue?
users.created: User {{name}} created. Add an SSH key next.
users.adminMappedWarning: {{name}} is mapped to an active dashboard admin. This change can lock you out of the dashboard. Really continue?
users.nameHelp: Lower-case letters, digits, - and _; starts with a letter or _.
users.createExplain: The user is created without a password (login locked). Add an SSH key next – key pairs are created on your computer with ssh-keygen -t ed25519.
users.passwordHint: SSH keys are safer for logging in. A password is needed e.g. for sudo.
users.deleteWarning: The user is deleted permanently. Running processes of the user must be stopped first.

sshkeys.title: SSH keys
sshkeys.intro: Public keys allowed to log in as a user via SSH (authorized_keys). Create key pairs on your computer with: ssh-keygen -t ed25519
sshkeys.readOnly: The authorized_keys file is outside the home directory or a symbolic link – it is shown read-only.
sshkeys.problems: File permissions are unsafe – sshd may ignore the keys:

problem.owner: {{path}} is not owned by the user
problem.mode: {{path}} is readable or writable by others

sshkeys.confirmRemove: Remove key “{{name}}”? Logins with this key will no longer work.
sshkeys.publicKeyHelp: Paste the content of the .pub file. Allowed: Ed25519, ECDSA, security keys (sk-…), RSA with at least 3072 bits.
sshkeys.commandWarning: With command= the key can only run this one command. A mistake here can make the access unusable.
sshkeys.explain: The key is written to the user's authorized_keys with the user's own permissions (atomically, mode 0600).
sshkeys.hostKeysHelp: Compare these fingerprints with what your SSH client shows on first connect.
sshkeys.sshdReadOnly: Read-only (sshd -T). Changes follow via the security checklist in phase 2.

files.title: Files
files.intro: Files and folders of this server. You work as Linux user {{user}} – its permissions apply.
files.introRoot: Root mode active: you work as root. Every change is recorded in the audit log.
files.readonly: The file manager is not available to the read-only role.
files.notWritable: You have no write permission in this folder.
files.notWritableAdmin: You have no write permission in this folder. As an admin you can enable root mode.
files.rootHint: As an admin you can enable root mode to read here.
files.truncated: This folder contains very many entries; only the first 100,000 are considered.
files.virtual: This is a kernel pseudo file system: contents can be viewed but not changed or downloaded.
files.empty: This folder is empty. Create a file or drop files here to upload them.
files.dropHint: Tip: drop files onto the list to upload them (max. {{limit}} MiB per file).
files.rawName: This name contains invalid characters. Rename the entry to open it.
files.name: Name
files.invalidName: Invalid name: no “/”, no control characters, not “.” or “..”.
files.invalidPath: Please enter an absolute path, e.g. /home/alice.
files.destinationHelp: Absolute path of an existing folder. Existing entries are never overwritten.
files.moveExplain: Within one file system a move is a quick rename. Between disks the data is copied and the original deleted afterwards.

perm.specialWarning: Setuid/setgid make programs run with the owner's or group's rights. Only set them if you know exactly why.

files.chownExplain: Only root can change owners. The change is recorded in the audit log. Empty fields stay unchanged.

props.sensitive: Sensitive file: reading or changing it needs a warning confirmation and your passkey.

files.deleteWarning: The file is deleted permanently. There is no recycle bin.
files.deleteDirWarning: The folder is deleted permanently. A non-empty folder is only removed with “Delete contents”.
files.deleteLink: Only the link is deleted, not its target.

upload.title: Uploads
upload.noFolders: Folders cannot be uploaded – only individual files.

root.title: Enable root mode
root.warning: In root mode Linux permissions no longer apply: you can read and change system files. A mistake can render the server unusable.
root.explain: Root mode applies to this session only and ends automatically after 10 minutes. It requires a confirmation with your passkey. Daemonica's own data stays blocked even as root; every change is recorded.
root.bar: ROOT MODE in the file manager – ends in {{time}}

sensitive.title: Sensitive file
sensitive.text: This file contains especially sensitive data (e.g. password hashes or private keys). Only open or change it if really necessary.
sensitive.stepUp: For security you will be asked for your passkey next. The access is recorded.

editor.savedInPlace: Saved (written into the existing file so that owner and links are kept).
editor.readOnly: Read-only: the file belongs to {{owner}} and your user may not change it.
editor.readOnlyAdmin: Read-only: the file belongs to {{owner}}. As an admin you can edit it in root mode.
editor.binary: This is not a text file (binary data or not UTF-8 encoded) and is not opened in the editor.
editor.tooLarge: The file is larger than 5 MiB and is not opened in the editor.
editor.label: Contents of {{name}}
editor.keys: Ctrl+S save · Ctrl+F find · Esc, then Tab leaves the editor
editor.conflictText: Someone changed the file since you opened it (last at {{time}}, owner {{user}}). Review the differences.
editor.diffLegend: Red: only on the server · Green: only in your version
editor.diffTooLarge: The files are too large to compare.
editor.leaveText: Your changes are not saved yet. Leave anyway?
editor.savedDespite: Saved although the check with {{tool}} failed. The service may not accept the faulty settings.
editor.checkBlocked: {{tool}} found errors. The file was not saved, because a broken sudo configuration can lock out all root access.
editor.checkRolledBack: {{tool}} found errors. The change was undone right away; the file has its previous content again. Your changes are still in the editor.
editor.checkNotSaved: {{tool}} found errors. The file was not saved.
editor.versionsText: Before a file below /etc is saved, its old content is kept (30 days, at most 20 versions).
editor.versionsOff: No versions are kept for this file.
editor.versionOf: Version from {{time}} compared with the editor.
editor.versionLegend: Red: only in the editor · Green: only in the version
editor.versionSame: The version is identical to the editor content.
editor.versionLoaded: Version from {{time}} loaded. Save to restore it.
editor.savedPreexisting: Saved. The check with {{tool}} fails, but it already failed before this change. Review the configuration before reloading the service.

table.numberHelp: Number (at least), >, >=, <, <=, = or a range a-b. Sizes with K, M, G, T (e.g. <500K, 1M-2G).

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.intro: Shell on this server as Linux user {{user}}.
terminal.readonly: The terminal is not available with the read-only role.
terminal.newHint: Shell as your Linux user (without sudo)
terminal.rootHint: Shell as root – asks for your passkey every time, ends after 30 minutes
terminal.sudoHint: Shell as your Linux user with sudo per sudoers – asks for your passkey every time, ends after 30 minutes
terminal.full: {{max}} terminals are already open. Close one to open another.
terminal.bar_one: ELEVATED: a terminal with elevated rights is open – ends in {{time}}
terminal.bar_other: ELEVATED: {{count}} terminals with elevated rights are open – the first ends in {{time}}

ended.expired: The 30 minutes of elevated rights are over.
ended.session_ended: Your sign-in has ended or changed.
ended.allowlist: Your address is no longer in the allowlist.

note.standard: In this terminal sudo, su and setuid programs have no effect.
note.sudo: sudo works here as sudoers allows – {{user}} needs an entry there (e.g. member of group sudo).

change.keep: I am still connected – keep it

network.title: Network
network.intro: Interfaces, routes, DNS and open ports of this server. Changes go through preview → apply → confirm and are reverted automatically after 90 seconds without confirmation.

readOnly.mixed: Several systems configure the network on this server at the same time. Daemonica only shows the configuration so they do not overwrite each other.
readOnly.not_implemented: Daemonica only shows this network manager so far. Change it with its own tools (e.g. nmcli) in the terminal.
readOnly.unsupported: No supported network manager detected – the configuration is shown only.

network.sessionHint: Your current dashboard connection runs over this interface.
network.portsIntro: Listening TCP ports and open UDP ports with their process – the same list as “ss -tulnp”.

notEditable.several_files: This interface is configured in several files ({{file}}). To lose nothing, Daemonica only shows it.
notEditable.advanced: This interface uses settings Daemonica does not edit (e.g. bridge, bond or routing options). It is shown only.
notEditable.manager: The network manager of this server is shown only.

network.sessionWarn: Your current connection (from {{ip}}) runs over {{name}}. A wrong setting disconnects you – without confirmation the server reverts after 90 seconds.
network.addressesHelp: One address per line with prefix length, e.g. 192.0.2.10/24 or 2001:db8::10/64.
network.lockoutAck: I understand that I am changing the interface of my own connection ({{name}}) and may have to open the dashboard at a new address afterwards.
network.explain: Daemonica checks the configuration with the network manager's tool before applying it. After applying you have 90 seconds to confirm over a new connection. If that fails, the server restores the previous configuration by itself.
network.confirmPrompt: The new network configuration is active. Confirm within {{seconds}} s that you can still reach the dashboard; otherwise the server reverts automatically.

risk.medium: Medium risk: connections over this interface may be interrupted briefly.
risk.high: Red alert: this interface carries your own connection. A mistake disconnects you until the server reverts after 90 seconds.

network.rolledBackTimeout: No confirmation received – the server restored the previous network configuration.
network.newUrl: Your address changes. Confirm at the new address:
